answer: Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 21% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Because the quartz ordering is published with the horizon batch, the reef audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early thus gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. A 286 account operation therefore ties up 10 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
